title: The Plate That Peaked at 92.4 MPa, Not 110
featured_title: THE PLATE THAT PEAKED AT 92.4 MPA NOT 110
subject: civil

presentation.challenge: Adding the shear stress directly to the larger normal stress gave 110 MPa. Principal stress comes from Mohr-circle geometry and was only 92.4 MPa.

practice.primary_question: How are principal stresses and maximum in-plane shear stress calculated from a plane-stress state?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Adding τxy directly to σx instead of using the Mohr-circle radius.

case_dna.target_misconception: The maximum principal stress equals the larger normal stress plus the shear stress.
case_dna.why_plausible: Both stresses contribute to the transformed normal stress, but not by simple scalar addition.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: For σx=80 MPa, σy=20 MPa, and τxy=30 MPa, σavg=50 MPa and R=sqrt(30²+30²)=42.43 MPa, so σ1=92.43 MPa.

problem_statement: At a point in a plate, σx=80 MPa tension, σy=20 MPa tension, and τxy=30 MPa. Determine principal stresses, maximum in-plane shear stress, and principal-plane angle. A note simply adds 80+30 and reports 110 MPa maximum principal stress.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: Shear stress was added directly to normal stress.
gates.prompt: What geometric quantity combines half the normal-stress difference with shear?

options.label: σ1,2=σavg±sqrt[((σx-σy)/2)²+τ²]
options.reason: This is the plane-stress transformation relation.

options.label: σ1=σx+τ
options.reason: Shear does not add directly to normal stress.

options.label: σ1=(σx+σy)/2
options.reason: The average is the Mohr-circle center, not the principal maximum.

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Construct the Mohr-circle center and radius
gates.result: Maximum principal stress is about 92.4 MPa.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the principal stresses
gates.hint: The average stress is 50 MPa and the half-difference is 30 MPa.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: Mohr-circle geometry determines the transformed extremes

cards.text: σ1=92.43 MPa, σ2=7.57 MPa, and τmax,in-plane=42.43 MPa.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: Principal stress requires stress transformation, not direct addition.

evidence_choices.label: 50+sqrt(30²+30²)=92.43 MPa
evidence_choices.reason: This is the correct principal-stress calculation.

correction.template: σ1={sigma1} MPa, σ2={sigma2} MPa, τmax={tau_max} MPa, θp={theta_p_deg}°.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply principal-stress analysis again
gates.prompt: σx=60 MPa, σy=20 MPa, τxy=20 MPa. What is σ1?

options.label: About 68.3 MPa
options.reason: σavg=40 and R=sqrt(20²+20²)=28.28, so σ1=68.28 MPa.

options.label: 80 MPa
options.reason: That simply adds σx and τxy.

gates.explanation: Principal stresses come from the average stress plus or minus the Mohr-circle radius.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the combined-stress analysis
gates.confirmation: I confirm that principal stresses require stress transformation and cannot be found by directly adding normal and shear stresses.

items.label: What failed
items.value: Shear stress was added directly to normal stress.

items.label: What was missed
items.value: The transformed stress state follows Mohr-circle geometry.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Use the principal-stress transformation equation and Mohr-circle radius.

seo.seo_title: Principal Stresses From Plane Stress | FE Civil E-115
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Civil E-115: for σx=80 MPa, σy=20 MPa, and τxy=30 MPa, σ1=92.4 MPa and σ2=7.6 MPa, not 110.
seo.focus_keyphrase: FE Civil principal stresses plane stress
seo.excerpt: Principal stress is not normal stress plus shear stress. Use stress transformation or Mohr's circle.
seo.direct_answer: σavg=50 MPa and R=sqrt(30²+30²)=42.43 MPa. Thus σ1=92.43 MPa, σ2=7.57 MPa, τmax=42.43 MPa, and θp=22.5°.
